Philosophy Quotes About Courage

Courage is often defined against fear: not fearlessness, but right action when fear is present. Classical and modern writers disagree about whether courage is mainly military, civic, or moral.

Quotes / About / Courage

15 quotations on courage

  1. It is worse to do injustice than to suffer it.
    Socrates
    Justice
  2. It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult.
    Seneca
    Courage
  3. He who has learned how to die has unlearned how to be a slave.
    Seneca
    Death
  4. Dare to know! Have the courage to use your own understanding!
    Immanuel Kant
    Enlightenment
  5. Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Self
  6. A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Authenticity
  7. Fear is the main source of superstition, and one of the main sources of cruelty. To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
    Bertrand Russell
    Fear
  8. The Master said: When you have faults, do not fear to correct them.
    Confucius
    Philosophy
  9. The courage to be is the courage to accept oneself as accepted in spite of being unacceptable.
    Paul Tillich
    Courage
  10. So too, by doing just acts we become just, by doing temperate acts temperate, and by doing brave acts brave.
    Aristotle
    Virtue
  11. The Master said: The wise are not perplexed; the humane are not anxious; the brave are not afraid.
    Confucius
    Wisdom
  12. To dare is to lose one’s footing momentarily. Not to dare is to lose oneself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Courage
  13. Courage is the self-affirmation of being in spite of the fact of nonbeing.
    Paul Tillich
    Courage
  14. Your silence will not protect you.
    Audre Lorde
    Language
  15. Relativism of that sort isn't a way to encourage conversation; it's just a reason to fall silent.
    Kwame Anthony Appiah
    Dialogue
